title: Fence the deprecated web gateway compatibility surface
description: After the gateway adapter seam is closed, reduce the residual web compatibility path in `src-ts/web/app.ts` to an explicitly bounded fallback so HTTP root forwarding and websocket workflow behavior remain opt-in compatibility logic rather than a parallel primary surface.

criteria: 1 deprecated HTTP root policy remains in `src-ts/web/app.ts`: default `410` response with validated forwarding only when `WEB_UI_FORWARD_URL` is explicitly set.
1 websocket compatibility policy remains opt-in and continues to advertise Desktop client or MCP Gateway as the primary path.
0 new runtime dependencies from `src-ts/web/app.ts` back into the core gateway integration bundle are introduced.
convergence.verification: npm --prefix src-ts run test -- tests/web/app.test.ts && npm --prefix src-ts run typecheck
convergence.definition_of_done: The deprecated web surface is explicitly bounded, aligns with the closed gateway integration boundary from `IMPL-001`, and the web compatibility tests plus typecheck pass.

implementation.title: Align compatibility behavior with the primary runtime boundary
implementation.description: Review root-route forwarding, websocket gating, and user-facing deprecation messaging in `src-ts/web/app.ts` against the Desktop plus MCP Gateway authority path established by the gateway module.

implementation.title: Remove residual ambiguity from the web fallback surface
implementation.description: Tighten the implementation so compatibility-only behavior stays explicit, does not imply a first-class web runtime, and does not reopen the broader compatibility seam closed in `IMPL-001`.

implementation.title: Lock the bounded behavior with existing tests
implementation.description: Refresh `src-ts/tests/web/app.test.ts` assertions to cover the final `410`, validated forwarding, and websocket gating behavior expected after the module closure.

notes: This task starts only after the gateway adapter boundary is explicit.
Keep the web surface as bounded compatibility only; do not reopen broader authority or runtime debates.
